title: Religious contributions to peace
log: 2026-10-29T12:14:29Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Religious contributions to peace
card: Members of different religions meet to talk, listen and build trust. It aims to reduce fear and misunderstanding between faith communities.
Religious groups give food, shelter, medical care and education to people in need, including people hurt by conflict. Easing hardship can reduce tension that leads to violence.
Religious leaders and groups speak out, protest and lobby governments to avoid or end war. They often base this on their teachings about peace and human dignity.
These three actions are different ways that religious people turn teachings about peace into work in the world.
draft.remember: Religious people work for peace by talking across faiths, giving aid and speaking out against war.

a.q: Leaders from a mosque, a synagogue and a church meet each month to share concerns and build trust. Which contribution to peace is this?
a.why: People from different religions meeting to talk and build trust is interfaith dialogue. It is not aid, because no goods or services are given, and it is not a campaign, because it does not target a war or a government.
a.clue: Look at who is meeting and what they are doing together.

b.q: A church agency in Sydney sends food and medical supplies to families who fled a war. How does this work contribute to peace?
opts: It eases hardship that can feed tension and violence
It brings leaders of different faiths together to talk
It pressures governments to end the war
It teaches refugees to meditate for inner peace
b.why: This is aid. Meeting basic needs can reduce the desperation that leads to conflict. It is not dialogue or a campaign, because it neither brings faiths together nor aims to change government policy, even though the agency could do those things too.
b.clue: Focus on what the agency is giving, not on what it might also do.

b.best: It eases hardship that can feed tension and violence
